text:
anya: quick RFC follow-up: proposing a split activation model for islanded registries + plugin bundles. gist: separate 'payload activation' from 'plugin activation' so operator can verify core artifacts before enabling runtime plugins. thoughts?

devon: can you sketch failure modes? is this just operator UX or changes to the onprem agent protocol? :thinking:

anya: both. agent handshake needs a new 'activation_phase' enum: PRE_ACTIVATE (payload only), PLUGIN_STAGE, PLUGIN_ACTIVATE. operator can approve PRE_ACTIVATE to let system boot, then selectively flip PLUGIN_ACTIVATE per-node. main win = reduce blast radius for plugin regressions.

liam: sounds ok but how do we handle signatures and attestation? we currently validate manifest sigs once before apply.

anya: proposal: payload envelope keeps current chained signatures. plugin bundle is a separate signed artifact with its own envelope version (v2) and its own certificate chain. agent verifies both independently. operator can choose to reject plugin v2 if old onprem policy requires v1 certs.

maya: what about dependencies between payload and plugin? some runtime changes require binary hooks in payload itself.

anya: agreed. require a small 'compat' section in payload manifest listing minimal plugin API level. at PRE_ACTIVATE we still check compat constraints and fail fast.

devon: how does this affect rollbacks? if plugin activation fails after payload pre-activated, we must fallback cleanly.

liam: fallback plan: agent maintains two activation markers in local state: active_payload_id, active_plugin_id. activation is a 2-phase commit with an idempotent apply and a reversible activation marker write. if plugin fails, agent clears active_plugin_id and signals operator: "plugin-activation-failed". payload stays active.

anya: exact. and include a quarantine window: plugins that fail more than N times are quarantined on that node until operator intervention.

infra-bot: note: alerting rule needed: plugin_activation_failures > 5 over 1h -> P3.

maya: storage footprint? extra artifacts means more disk usage on air-gapped nodes. we have many customers with limited spare disk.

anya: we'd recommend a shared plugin cache on the node or a local registry. default pruning policy: keep last 2 payloads + last 3 plugins. config: operator can tune retention.

devon: operator workflow: how does someone promote plugin to all nodes?

anya: operator uses console or CLI to 'promote-plugin' which sets a cluster-level desired_plugin_id and starts a canary rollout by default. rollout policy reuse: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with health checks tied to plugin_probe endpoints.

liam: healthchecks: we need a standard plugin probe contract. short HTTP path /_plugin_probe that returns JSON {"status":"ok","version":"x"}. agents must fallback to HTTP polling during PLUGIN_STAGE.

maya: does this complicate air-gapped upgrades where there's no operator console?

anya: in air-gapped mode operator still runs CLI against the bastion. CLI pushes desired_plugin_id into the cluster operator manifest (yaml) which gets reconciled by the operator inside the VPC. so same flow, just manual push.

devon: corner case: if a node is offline during plugin promote, it may later try to activate an old plugin leading to drift. how handle reconcilers?

liam: agents should compare active_plugin_id vs cluster_desired_plugin_id on reconcile. if mismatch, agent should fetch plugin artifact (if available) and attempt activation. if artifact missing, log and set state=WAITING_FOR_ARTIFACT. operator can inspect node-level status.

anya: also add a 'compat-fallback' policy: if artifact missing for >72h and node is critical, operator can opt-in to skip plugin activation and keep payload-only mode. config flag: allow_payload_only=true.

maya: telemetry: want to see per-plugin activation latency, failure rates, and node-level quarantine counts. add metrics: plugin_activate_attempts_total, plugin_activate_success_total, plugin_quarantine_count.

infra-bot: added metric stubs to the metrics board.

devon: security: plugin bundles may run native code. do we sandbox?

anya: yes — enforce SELinux/AppArmor profile for plugin execs and run plugins in an isolated container runtime by default. for older onprem installs without container runtime, deny native plugin activation unless operator explicitly enables legacy_plugins=true.

liam: any changes to the network protocol between operator <> agent? small extension to the operator API: POST /v1/activation with body {"phase":"PLUGIN_STAGE","id":"..."}. agent responds with 202 + operation_id. we already have similar endpoints so minimal change.

maya: docs and upgrade notes needed. this is a behavioral change for ops teams.

anya: I'll draft an RFC section with: protocol changes, manifest compat schema (compat.version int), plugin envelope v2 spec, agent state machine w/ transitions, rollback flow, metrics, and operator CLI UX.

devon: can you include an example manifest diff?

anya: sure. example: 
```
manifest:
  id: payload-2026-04-12
  compat_api: 3
  plugins:
    - id: plugin-logger-v7
      sig: sha256:abcd...
      envelope_version: 2
      probes:
        - path: /_plugin_probe
          timeout: 2s
```

liam: looks good. add note about signature rotation: operator must be able to rotate plugin verification keys separately. we need a keystore extension in operator manifest: plugin_verifiers: [ ... ]

anya: yes. I'll add a key rotation playbook and a migration tool to map old v1 keys -> v2 verifiers.

ops: heads-up for support: this will create new node states we'll need to document (WAITING_FOR_ARTIFACT, PLUGIN_QUARANTINED, PLUGIN_ROLLING_BACK). please sync with SRE runbooks.

maya: final Q: rollout speed—are we comfortable with per-node sequential activation or should agent do parallel plugin activation across CPU cores?

liam: activation is mostly atomic file ops + container start, parallelizing per-plugin on a node is ok but complexity isn't worth it for now. keep single-threaded activation per-agent with queue.

anya: thanks all — next steps: I'll post RFC addendum with exact schema + operator CLI examples. tagging @devon @liam for review in 48h. :thumbsup:

devon: ack, will review.

liam: ack.

ops: noted, prepping runbook boilerplate.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: created tracking issue: #INF-1289
